issues.description: The problem statement first describes the SealSaloon.stock as a final instance attribute initialized in the constructor, but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all SealSaloon instances). This contradiction about whether stock is an instance final field or a static field will confuse students when implementing SealSaloon.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent: clearly state that the stock attribute is static (shared across all SealSaloon instances) if that is the intended design, or change the solution to use an instance final stock if the stock should be per-instance. Update the UML, textual description, and any notes so they all consistently indicate 'private static final Stock stock' (or 'private final Stock stock' if instance-level is intended).

issues.description: The UML and textual specification state that calculateRemainingOrderNumber() should return an int representing the number of remaining orders, but the provided solution implements calculateRemainingOrderNumber() as a void method that prints order numbers instead. This return-type/behavior mismatch will confuse students about the expected signature and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide on the intended API: either change the problem statement/UML to indicate the method prints status and returns void, or change the solution (and tests) so calculateRemainingOrderNumber() returns an int (e.g., the number of remaining orders) and optionally provide a separate method to print order numbers. Ensure the method signature in UML, description, template, and solution all match.
